issues.body: The run block uses `set -uo pipefail` rather than `set -euo pipefail`. Consequently, a nonzero exit from `alert_route.py --self-test` or `retriage-alert.py --self-test` does not stop the step; the following command runs, and if that final command returns zero the step is green. A broken routing or alert regression can therefore pass the production alert job despite the explicit preflight checks.
issues.fix_hint: Enable errexit for this run block (or explicitly chain/check each command) so either self-test failure prevents the emitter invocation from producing an apparently successful step.
issues.title: Alert script and router self-test failures are swallowed

issues.body: The only alert step has `continue-on-error: true`. When `retriage-alert.py` returns 1 because listing, creating, editing, commenting, or closing failed, GitHub permits the job to complete successfully. That contradicts the script's stated fail-loud contract and leaves the original silent-outage mode intact: retriage can fail while its alert delivery also fails, yet no alert job/run failure is exposed as a durable signal.
issues.fix_hint: Remove step-level `continue-on-error` so delivery failures make `retriage-alert` fail. Job isolation is already provided by the separate `needs`/`always()` alert job; failing this job cannot retroactively affect the retriage sweep.
issues.title: continue-on-error makes hard alert failures invisible at job level

verdict.summary: The new alert path is not actually fail-loud. Its workflow shell deliberately omits errexit, so either self-test can fail without preventing the emitter from running, and the whole step is marked continue-on-error, which converts even a checked emitter failure into a successful job conclusion. This defeats the stated purpose of making a broken retriage alert leg observable. The routing, decision matrix, dedupe marker, and wiring tests are otherwise substantive.
